contentPrompt.registerNote: Spanish register: a crew lead or foreman speaking to a crew uses the plural ustedes imperative (corten, revisen, traigan); speaking to ONE person (a customer, a patient, one worker) uses usted. Use Mexican / US Spanish as working tradespeople and staff in the United States actually say it, including a common loanword when that is what people say on the job (troca, yarda, mopear) but only when it is standard job-site usage. Write ¿ and ¡ properly.
contentPrompt.nearFuture: ir a + infinitive in Spanish, going to in English
contentPrompt.regionRule: Use one regional variety per lesson, matching the setting, and never mix them: Spain uses euros, billete, camarero, comisaría, franquicia; Mexico and Latin America use pesos, boleto, mesero, deducible.
contentPrompt.reportedSpeech: El jefe dice: Revisen la cuchilla.

directSpeech.good: El jefe dice: Revisen la cuchilla.
directSpeech.bad: El jefe dice: Revisen la cuchilla, y Marta corta.

contentPrompt.infinitive: the Spanish infinitive, e.g. cortar, or reflexive lavarse
contentPrompt.formsNote: , except the reflexive pronoun for reflexive verbs ("me lavo", "nos lavamos"). All five forms must be different and must be correct: nosotros ends in -mos, ellos/ustedes ends in -n, tú ends in -s. Mark stem changes in "note" (o to ue)
